senses.sense_definition: A medium-sized modern warship, typically smaller than a destroyer, used for escort and anti-submarine duties.

examples.text: The navy deployed a guided missile <w>frigate</w> to patrol international waters.
During naval exercises, the modern <w>frigate</w> tracked and intercepted simulated enemy submarines.

senses.sense_definition: A fast, three-masted sailing warship of the 18th and 19th centuries, equipped with a single main gun deck and used for reconnaissance and cruising.

examples.text: The swift sailing <w>frigate</w> outran the enemy fleet and delivered the urgent dispatch.
Historians studied the restored wooden <w>frigate</w> to learn how sailors lived in the eighteenth century.

traits.comment: refers to a historical type of sailing vessel

senses.sense_definition: A type of combat spacecraft designed for scouting, escort, or screening against smaller craft.

examples.text: The assault fleet positioned each heavy <w>frigate</w> to screen the main carrier from enemy fighters.
In the science fiction game, your first command is a lightly armed patrol <w>frigate</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A frigatebird, a large seabird known for its long wings and pirate-like habit of stealing food from other birds.

examples.text: High above the tropical island, a solitary <w>frigate</w> wheeled gracefully against the clouds.
We watched the black <w>frigate</w> harass a booby until it dropped the fish it had caught.
